details: Post-Gupta fragmentation saw King Harshavardhana (606–647 CE) of Vardhana Dynasty establish order with capital at Kannauj
Documented by court poet Banabhatta (Harshacharita) and Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Xuanzang who studied at Nalanda University
Harsha held grand quinquennial assemblies at Prayag for religious discourse and public charity distribution
evidence_or_examples: Xuanzang's travelogue describing Nalanda University's multi-storeyed monasteries and strict entrance examinations

details: Chalukyas of Badami (Vatapi): Pulakeshin II famously defeated Harsha on the Narmada River; patrons of Aihole, Badami, and Pattadakal temples
Pallavas of Kanchipuram: Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I built rock-cut rathas and structural Shore Temple at Mamallapuram
Rashtrakutas of Manyakheta: Prominent rulers Krishna I and Amoghavarsha I (author of Kavirajamarga); excavated Kailashanatha Temple at Ellora
evidence_or_examples: Pulakeshin II's Aihole Inscription composed by court poet Ravikirti recording victory over Harsha

branches.theme: Imperial Conflict, Land Economy, and Administration

details: Centuries-long strategic conflict (8th–10th century) among Palas (Bengal), Gurjara-Pratiharas (Malwa/Rajasthan), and Rashtrakutas (Deccan)
Fought for political control over Kannauj, the imperial symbol of northern sovereignty and gateway to Gangetic trade wealth
evidence_or_examples: Repeated shifts in Kannauj's control among Dharmapala (Pala), Vatsaraja (Pratihara), and Dhruva (Rashtrakuta)

details: Brahmadeya: Tax-free land or entire villages granted to Brahmins; Devadana: Land granted to temples; recorded on copper-plate charters with royal seals
Samanta System: Subordinate chieftains/feudatories who provided military contingents, paid annual tribute, and attended royal courts
Local Assemblies: Sabha (assembly of Brahmin property owners in Brahmadeya villages) and Ur (general village assembly in non-Brahmin villages)
evidence_or_examples: Uttaramerur inscriptions detailing qualifications, sub-committees (variyams), and Kudavolai secret ballot voting for village governance

details: Pallava Art: Cave temples, monolithic Pancha Rathas, and structural Shore Temple at Mamallapuram
Rashtrakuta Art: Monolithic Kailashanatha Temple (Cave 16) at Ellora excavated top-down from a basalt mountain cliff under Krishna I
Chalukya Art: Temple complexes at Pattadakal combining Nagara and Dravida architectural styles
evidence_or_examples: Ellora Cave 16 showing top-down rock chiseling technique removing over 200,000 tons of rock

details: Rise of South Indian Bhakti devotionalism: Shaivite Nayanars and Vaishnavite Alvars composing emotional Tamil devotional hymns
Pala patrons established renowned Mahayana Buddhist learning centers: Vikramashila, Odantapuri, and Somapura Mahavihara
evidence_or_examples: Devotional poetry collections: Tevaram (Nayanars) and Divya Prabandham (Alvars)
